channel.title: Credit to Keys — own a home without the bank's permission
channel.description: Honest creative-finance and credit education from Greg Jimenez. Education, not advice.

item.title: A 500 credit score blocks a bank. It does not block owning a home
item.description:
Those are two different sentences, and confusing them costs people years. A low score blocks conventional loans and the best rates. It does not block taking title, seller financing, or collecting rent.
I rebuilt mine from the 400s while I bought. The order I used is in the free guide.
Free guide, no email: egesystems.com/keys Education and coaching, not financial, legal, tax, or credit advice. My own results; individual results vary.

item.title: "I need 20% down" is the myth that keeps renters renting
item.description:
Conventional lending taught everyone one path. It is not the only one. Sellers can finance. Existing loans can sometimes be taken over. Partners bring the capital.
None of it is magic and none of it is guaranteed — but most people have never even seen the other doors. The guide walks them.
Free guide, no email: egesystems.com/keys Education and coaching, not financial, legal, tax, or credit advice. My own results; individual results vary.

item.title: What is seller financing, in one line?
item.description:
The person selling the house acts as the bank, and you pay them directly over time instead of qualifying at a lender.
It is not right for every deal or every seller, and terms vary. But when a bank says no, this is one of the doors worth understanding.

item.title: Your credit score is not one number — it is a few habits
item.description:
Payment history and how much of your limits you use do most of the heavy lifting. Understand those two and the number stops feeling like a mystery.
This is education, not a promise of any specific score. But you cannot fix what you do not understand.

item.title: You can shop for a home while you rebuild
item.description:
Waiting until your credit is "perfect" to even learn the game is backwards. Learn the strategies now, work the credit in parallel, and be ready when a deal shows up.
That is the whole idea behind the guide — start before you feel ready.

item.title: Only dispute what is actually wrong
item.description:
If something on your report is genuinely inaccurate, you have every right to dispute it. That is it — no tricks, no promises to erase real history.
Anyone promising to delete accurate accounts is selling you a problem. Honest education only.

item.title: Why a bank says no but a seller says yes
item.description:
A bank scores you against a rigid box. A motivated seller scores you against their own goal — getting the property sold on terms that work.
Different decision-maker, different rules. Understanding that is half the game.

item.title: Credit utilization: the lever most people ignore
item.description:
Carrying balances close to your limits can weigh on your score even when you pay on time. Keeping them lower is one of the simpler things within your control.
General education, not a guarantee — but it is a lever worth knowing.

item.title: "No money down" — the honest version
item.description:
It rarely means zero dollars from anyone. It usually means the money comes from somewhere other than your own savings — a seller, a partner, existing financing.
I will not sell you a fantasy. I will show you how the pieces actually fit.

item.title: The order I did it in matters more than any one trick
item.description:
People want the single hack. The results came from a sequence — understand credit, learn the strategies, line up the pieces, then move.
That sequence is what the free guide lays out. My own results; yours will differ.

item.title: Renting is not throwing money away — but it can be a trap
item.description:
Rent buys you a place to live, and that has real value. The trap is renting for a decade because you assumed the only path to owning was one you could not qualify for.
There are other paths. Worth learning before another lease renews.
Free guide, no email: egesystems.com/keys Education and coaching, not financial, legal, tax, or credit advice. My own results; individual results vary.

item.title: First step is not a lender. It is understanding your options
item.description:
Most people start by getting told no, then give up. Start instead by learning what is actually possible — conventional, seller-financed, partnered, and more.
The guide is free and there is no email wall. Just the map.
Free guide, no email: egesystems.com/keys Education and coaching, not financial, legal, tax, or credit advice. My own results; individual results vary.

item.title: Why would a seller ever agree to this?
item.description:
Newer investors ask this constantly. The answer is that not every seller is optimizing for price. Some are optimizing for time, or for relief.
Behind on payments. Relocated and carrying two housing costs. Inherited a property four hours away. Listed for months until the agent's contract ran out.
Not every seller says yes, and most will not. But the ones who do are solving a different problem than the one you assumed.
Free guide, no email: egesystems.com/keys Education and coaching, not financial, legal, tax, or credit advice. My own results; individual results vary.

item.title: The due-on-sale clause, explained straight
item.description:
Most mortgages contain a clause letting the lender call the balance due if the property changes hands. People online will tell you it never gets enforced. That is not a promise anyone can make to you.
It is a real risk that real investors weigh, disclose, and plan around. Anyone who tells you it is a non-issue is selling you confidence, not information.
Free guide, no email: egesystems.com/keys Education and coaching, not financial, legal, tax, or credit advice. My own results; individual results vary.

item.title: Reserves matter more than the down payment
item.description:
The money that gets people through is not the money that gets them in. A water heater, a vacancy, a tenant who stops paying — those arrive whether or not you budgeted for them.
A smaller down payment with cash left over is often steadier than the reverse. There is no universal right number, but zero is the one that ends deals.
Free guide, no email: egesystems.com/keys Education and coaching, not financial, legal, tax, or credit advice. My own results; individual results vary.

item.title: The balloon payment is the number to look at
item.description:
Seller-financed deals often carry one: a date when the remaining balance comes due in full.
That is not automatically bad. It is only bad when nobody planned for it. Know the date, know the amount, and know what you intend to do when it arrives — refinance, sell, or renegotiate.
A deal you cannot exit is not a deal. It is a deadline.
Free guide, no email: egesystems.com/keys Education and coaching, not financial, legal, tax, or credit advice. My own results; individual results vary.

item.title: House hacking, in plain terms
item.description:
Live in part of a property and rent the rest. A duplex, a room, a converted garage where it is legal.
It is not glamorous and it costs you privacy. But it is one of the few approaches where the property helps carry its own cost while you live in it. Rules vary by city — check yours before you count on it.
Free guide, no email: egesystems.com/keys Education and coaching, not financial, legal, tax, or credit advice. My own results; individual results vary.

item.title: How to look at a rental in ten minutes
item.description:
What does it rent for. What does the loan cost. What do taxes and insurance run. What is set aside for repairs and vacancy. What is left.
If what is left is thin, the deal does not get better because you want it to. This is a rough screen, not an appraisal — but it kills bad deals fast, and that is most of the work.
Free guide, no email: egesystems.com/keys Education and coaching, not financial, legal, tax, or credit advice. My own results; individual results vary.

item.title: The paperwork protects both sides
item.description:
Handshake deals are where creative finance earns its bad reputation. The documents exist so that both people know what happens if something goes wrong.
Get a real closing. Use a title company or an attorney in your state. If someone pressures you to skip that step, that pressure is the information.
Free guide, no email: egesystems.com/keys Education and coaching, not financial, legal, tax, or credit advice. My own results; individual results vary.

item.title: What actually ends most first deals
item.description:
Not interest rates. Not the market. Usually it is running out of money mid-repair, or a timeline nobody wrote down, or a partner who understood the split differently.
Boring failures, all of them preventable on paper before anyone signs.
Free guide, no email: egesystems.com/keys Education and coaching, not financial, legal, tax, or credit advice. My own results; individual results vary.

item.title: A hard inquiry is not what is holding you back
item.description:
People avoid applying because they fear the inquiry. Inquiries are a small factor and they fade.
What carries far more weight is payment history and how much of your available credit you are using. This is general education, not a promise about your specific score — but the thing most people worry about is rarely the thing costing them.
Free guide, no email: egesystems.com/keys Education and coaching, not financial, legal, tax, or credit advice. My own results; individual results vary.

item.title: You can build credit without taking on new debt
item.description:
Paying down balances you already carry moves utilization. Keeping old accounts open preserves history. Paying on time, every time, is the one that matters most.
None of these are tricks and none produce a guaranteed number. They are habits, and habits are the part you control.
Free guide, no email: egesystems.com/keys Education and coaching, not financial, legal, tax, or credit advice. My own results; individual results vary.

item.title: "Creative" does not mean a loophole
item.description:
It means structuring a purchase with terms instead of only with a bank. Seller financing, taking over payments where permitted, partnering.
It is all disclosed, documented, and legal when done right. If a strategy only works when somebody is not told about it, that is not creative finance. That is a problem waiting.
Free guide, no email: egesystems.com/keys Education and coaching, not financial, legal, tax, or credit advice. My own results; individual results vary.

item.title: The part nobody posts about
item.description:
The months of learning. The offers that go nowhere. The seller who says yes and then changes their mind at the table.
I rebuilt my credit and bought while I did it, and it was slower and less cinematic than any video makes it look. My own results, and yours will differ. But slow and real beats fast and imaginary.
